body.statement: On \(\mathcal B_0\), \(P_{A=0}(B=b)=P(B=b)\) for every compatible model, whereas \(P_{A=1}(B=1)\) is not identified. For the latter claim, take \(H\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), set \(A=0\), let the functional node satisfy \(D=A\), and set \(B=H\) on the reached row \((A,D)=(0,0)\) in both models; on the intervention-exposed row \((A,D)=(1,1)\), set \(B=0\) in the first model and \(B=1\) in the second. The models have the identical exact-support observed law \(P(A=0,D=0,B=b)=1/2\) and respective targets zero and one. Ordinary ID fails for the latent bow remaining after accounting for the directed paths. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination, under its stated separability and parent conditions, leaves that unidentified bow, while Theorem 18 is inapplicable because its treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\) includes \(\Pr(A=1)>0\), which the declared support contradicts. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 prove soundness only for formula-returning algorithms under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law; \(\mathcal B_0\) instead retains \(1\in\Omega_A\) as a valid intervention state while declaring \(P(A=1)=0\), so it is outside their input regime. Thus this exact functional-support pattern is strictly resolved by the proposed support trichotomy on a residual regime not covered by those comparators.
body.justification: The pattern exposes, on the smallest latent bow, both the supported state-specific formula branch and an exact-support rational NONID branch.
body.gap: Ordinary ID gives only bow failure. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 elimination of \(D\), under its separability and parent conditions, leaves the bow, and Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem separates the supported and unsupported intervention values on this declared structural-zero face. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound identification results for CSI and state-alphabet constraints under strict observational positivity, not a completeness or exact-support countermodel result for a valid treatment state assigned zero observational mass.
body.consumer: The pattern is a unit test requiring a support-aware implementation to return \(P(B=b)\) for \(A=0\) and an exact two-model certificate for \(A=1\).
